newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria domestic debt up at 2.8 trln levs Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria domestic debt up at 2.8 trln levs Feb 28.

text.p: Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 1,099 billion levs in February to 2.778 trillion levs because of the sharp lev fall and new government securities issued to finance public spending, Finance ministry figures showed.

"Internal debt rose some 65 percent last month mainly because of the lev fall, which boosted the lev price of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds and deposit guarantee bonds," a finance ministry official told Reuters.

Some 1,053 billion levs of the rise were due to the lev depreciation, figures showed. The lev fell to 2,045.5 per dollar on February 28 from 1,021.9 on January 31 in the central bank daily dollar fixing used in the calculations.
It traded near 1,600 per dollar on the local interbank market on Tuesday.
Net sales of government securities in February totalled about 58 billion levs, figures showed. @

Finance ministry's direct loans from the Bulgarian National Bank and the State Savings Bank fell by 12.3 billion levs to 138.8 billion levs in February as the ministry repaid all short-term loans and made partial payments on long-term borrowings, figures showed.

The ministry issued $79.2 million of floater coupon T-bonds last year to guarantee foreign currency deposits of companies and individuals in five local banks, against which the central bank has filed insolvency suits. @
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued two years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.

The total par value of dollar-denominated bad debt bonds in circulation at end-February was $949.8 million and lev-denominated bonds amounted to around 20 billion levs. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
